clue.text: Grand loan for each one inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the second piece goes within the first piece

parts.note: a sub is a small advance or loan, as against wages
per means for each one, as in 'a pound per head'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a large loan shared out so that each person gets one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like a thousand pounds to go with the loan, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and superb are both adjectives of high praise meaning magnificent.

clue.text: University, commended, is put on a higher level

parts.note: to commend someone is to praise them

explanation.surface: A university, praised by others, is promoted in the rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something raised up has been lifted or elevated to a higher position.

clue.text: Such abstention points to Conservative split over a Liberal

parts.note: E is east, one compass point
S is south, another compass point
to hew wood is to split it with an axe

explanation.surface: A political tale: abstention signals a Tory party divided over a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the C and HEW sit before A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Eschewing something is deliberately avoiding it, a kind of abstaining.

clue.text: Like an early bath?

parts.note: an infant's first ceremonial washing in church, the christening, is the earliest bath of all

explanation.surface: A sports-style phrase about being sent off early to the changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An early bath' is British sporting slang for being sent off; here it is a christening font.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the sacrament of christening, in which a child is washed with holy water.

clue.text: In which churchwardens stand out?

parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe, and pipes stand upright in a holder

explanation.surface: Asks where the parish officials of a church are prominent.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a long clay pipe, so this is a smoker's stand, not a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand for storing tobacco pipes holds long clay smoking pipes upright.

clue.text: Noted fairy tale re pedant who felt ill-treated

indicators.note: ill-treated means these words are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fairy tale about a pedant who felt badly used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to musical notes: Prokofiev's piece for narrator and orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev's orchestral story for children is a musical folk tale with a narrator.

clue.text: Vessel put into orbit

parts.note: the orbit is the bony socket of the eye, and the vessel is a little cup filled with lotion held against it

explanation.surface: Sounds like a spacecraft launched into orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orbit' suggests space; it is the eye socket.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup for bathing the eye is held against the socket to rinse it.

clue.text: Star sign of Daisy is last in book

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of the word book

explanation.surface: A horoscope question about the zodiac sign of a girl called Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star sign' is not the zodiac but the printed star symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol shaped like a little star marks a footnote.

clue.text: Reminder to control drink in Japan

parts.note: to keep animals or a house is to control or manage them
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A reminder to limit how much one drinks while in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento kept to recall a person or occasion serves as a reminder.

clue.text: Lunatic taking one drug after another

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A madman taking one drug after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric, crazy person, a madman.

clue.text: Square seat

definitions.meaning: to square a debt or argument

explanation.definitionFit: Settling a bill squares it; and an old wooden bench with arms is also so named.

clue.text: More convenient hour to rest, right?

parts.note: an hour is a time
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: Asks whether a better hour to have a rest would be right.
explanation.definitionFit: Timely means opportune, well-judged, so the comparative means more opportune.

clue.text: Tweed boatman on the Thames…

definitions.meaning: a cloth hand-woven in the Outer Hebrides gives its name to this tweed
one of the rowers in Jerome K Jerome's Three Men in a Boat, set on the Thames

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue but is only joining the two surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Scottish tweed bears the island's name, as does a character who rowed in Jerome's comic novel.

clue.text: …has to check on his mad manoeuvre

indicators.note: manoeuvre tells us the letters are moved around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The boatman has to keep an eye on his crazy manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' here is a verb: to rebuke or reprove.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to reprimand, to rebuke someone for a fault.

clue.text: One who has a scooping action will get a duck

definitions.text: One who has a scooping action
definitions.meaning: someone who digs with a spade-like implement
a dabbling duck with a broad spatulate bill

explanation.definitionFit: Someone using a spade to scoop earth, and a broad-billed dabbling duck, share the name.

clue.text: Favourite language, next to Latin

parts.note: Ido is an artificial language derived from Esperanto

explanation.surface: A preferred language placed beside Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite person adored by fans is a hero or star.

clue.text: Maxim'S sincere flatterer?

parts.note: the proverb says copying is the sincerest form of flattery, so one who copies is the sincere flatterer

explanation.surface: Asks who honestly praises a man named Maxim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim' looks like a name; it is the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier, according to the proverb, flatters most sincerely of all.

clue.text: Numbers in order for ring-road in a London system, initially

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of the words that follow it

explanation.surface: Numbers along the London ring road, in order.
explanation.definitionFit: First, second and third are numbers expressing position in a sequence.

clue.text: Destination of the Young Pretender's speedboat?

definitions.text: Destination of the Young Pretender's speedboat?

parts.words: Destination of the Young Pretender's speedboat?
parts.note: the ... Boat Song begins 'Speed, bonnie boat' and tells of Bonnie Prince Charlie fleeing over the sea

explanation.surface: Asks where Bonnie Prince Charlie's fast motor boat was heading.
explanation.walkthrough: The Young Pretender is Charles Edward Stuart, who fled to a Hebridean island in 1746.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebridean island to which Flora MacDonald carried the fugitive prince.

clue.text: Band saw, perhaps, for making light work

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder
a saw is an example of a tool

explanation.surface: A band saw is just the thing to make a job easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light work' means work on lights, windows: a brush for painting window frames. 'Band saw' is a decoy single item.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow painter's brush is used for the glazing bars of window frames.

clue.text: Most modern toy guns point all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: The latest toy guns aim in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The newest or most recent is the least aged.

clue.text: Section of couplet Horace used in profusion

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a Horatian couplet was used abundantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'used in profusion' as the definition, but only 'profusion' (a noun) matches; 'used in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A profusion is an abundance, an excess.

clue.text: Start playing with it and drop catch!

indicators.note: Start picks the first letter of playing

parts.note: to fall is to drop

explanation.surface: A cricket coach's exasperated cry: start playing properly and you drop a catch!
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' is a noun meaning a hidden snag, not the cricket kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden snag or trap, a hidden danger.

clue.text: Rodin's pensive sort of sitter

indicators.note: sort of signals the letters are sorted into a different order

explanation.surface: A sculptor's sad-looking model, like the figure in The Thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodin was French, so 'pensive' is wanted in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French adjective means sad or melancholy.

clue.text: Great seal needed for this size of, paper?

definitions.meaning: the largest seal species is named after a huge animal
a large traditional paper size, about 23 by 28 inches

explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'of' is an OCR slip; the page prints 'size of paper?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant seal of southern seas, and an old large size of drawing paper, share the name.

clue.text: Roman emperor knocking back a drink in town

indicators.note: in places the turned drink inside the abbreviation for town

parts.note: TN is the abbreviation for town

indicators.note: knocking back reads the phrase a drink in the reverse direction

parts.note: a jar is a drink, usually a pint of beer

explanation.surface: An emperor downing a drink in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' is drinking slang, but here it turns the phrase 'a drink' round; 'in' then sets that inside the town abbreviation. A jar is British slang for a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: He ruled Rome from AD 98 to 117 and built a famous column.

clue.text: Spectator who sees only one side of the game?

definitions.text: Spectator who sees only one side of the game?

parts.words: Spectator who sees only one side of the game?
parts.note: the saying is that the bystander sees most of the game; here the play is on the cricket on side

explanation.surface: A partial spectator watching a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The on side is one half of a cricket field, so the word splits as 'on' plus one who looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander watches events without taking part.

clue.text: New lease for a bit of a climber

indicators.note: New signals that the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new lease granted for a mountaineer, in part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' is a rambling rose, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing rose bears foliage, so a leaf from it is one part of the plant.

clue.text: Tell revealing half of core at the last minute

indicators.note: half of takes the final two of the four letters in the word core

parts.note: late means at the last minute

explanation.surface: Telling a secret by revealing half the core story very late.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate or recount it.
